---
title: "Sources and reading"
---

## Foundational reading

### V. I. Blagodatskikh — Introduction to Optimal Control

Primary reference for the opening part of the course:
linear controlled systems, reachable sets, and minimum-time
control.

The exact edition and lecture/page references will be specified
as individual lectures are prepared.

### Lawrence C. Evans — An Introduction to Mathematical Optimal Control Theory

Complementary reading on optimal control, the maximum principle,
dynamic programming, and differential games.

[Author-hosted lecture notes](https://math.berkeley.edu/~evans/control.course.pdf)

## Differential games

### Tamer Başar and Geert Jan Olsder — Dynamic Noncooperative Game Theory

Reference for dynamic games, information patterns,
equilibrium concepts, and pursuit–evasion.

### Rufus Isaacs — Differential Games

Classical geometric perspective on differential games
and pursuit–evasion.

### N. N. Krasovskii and A. I. Subbotin — Game-Theoretical Control Problems

Reference for positional strategies and guaranteed outcomes.

### A. A. Chikrii — Conflict-Controlled Processes

Reference for resolving functions, constructive pursuit,
and multiplayer problems.

### B. N. Pshenichnyi and V. V. Ostapenko — Differential Games

Companion reference for the constructive pursuit tradition.

## Pursuit–evasion survey

Isaac E. Weintraub, Meir Pachter, and Eloy Garcia,
*An Introduction to Pursuit-evasion Differential Games*.

Used as a map of pursuit–evasion problems and a source
of detailed cooperative-pursuit examples.

[arXiv record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.05013)

## Attribution

Individual lectures will identify their principal sources,
including specific sections or pages where possible.

Adapted arguments, examples, and exercises will be marked.
Numerical experiments and independently developed figures
will be distinguished from results established in the literature.
